articles.title: When in doubt, flail about
articles.summary: When you’re working in an unclear situation — you have no clear guidance, or you don’t know what will help — the best course of action is often just to flail about. This sounds counter-intuitive. Wouldn’t it be better to be cautious and wait until you have a better understanding of what’s going on? Typically not. This is definitely dangerous advice. articles.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
articles.summary: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. articles.title: Ladybird's first alpha release
articles.summary: Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. articles.title: Quoting Ravi Vakil
articles.summary: Alessandro Masullo has a proposed proof of [Generalized Riemann Hypothesis], and Brian Conrad has been looking closely at it for months and gave extensive feedback which is being incorporated, and it is so far looking good. It is all human, with no AI. The hope was to bring Alessandro to Stanford for a year to polish the writing and then announce it after running it by enough people. Now it seems best to put out the current draft. — Ravi Vakil, Hurried Announcement: Alessandro Masullo GRH
